questions.q: The org does not use Entitlements or Milestones. How can you still measure SLA compliance?
options: It is impossible without milestones
Use a row-level formula for resolution hours, flag cases over the target for their priority, and summarize the flag
Count the number of agents on the team
Read compliance from the Origin field
questions.explain: A row-level breach flag summed and divided by record count gives compliance from fields you already have.

questions.q: Overall compliance is 88 percent, but High-priority cases breach about 23 percent of the time. What does this show?
options: The overall number is always the most useful one
High priority is the safest group
Grouping by priority can reveal that the most urgent cases fail most often
Breach rates cannot be grouped
questions.explain: Headline rates can mask problem segments. Always break compliance down by the dimension that drives the target.

questions.q: What should you do before interpreting a high escalation rate as poor team performance?
options: Assume it is the agents' fault
Delete the escalated cases
Ignore it because escalations are unimportant
Find out how escalation happens, since rules or a healthy process may route hard cases upward on purpose
questions.explain: Escalation can be automatic or a deliberate process step. Context determines whether the number signals a problem.

questions.q: High priority: 52 of 186 cases escalated. What is the escalation rate, roughly?
options: 28 percent
5 percent
52 percent
186 percent
questions.explain: 52 divided by 186 is about 0.28, or 28 percent.

questions.q: Why write SLA targets on your definitions sheet before building reports?
options: Reports cannot run without them
Without a stated target, calling a case slow is just an opinion, and readers cannot check your compliance figure
Salesforce enforces them automatically
They make dashboards load faster
questions.explain: A target turns speed into a measurable promise and lets others verify your numbers.
